dg.title: David and Goliath
lines: Every morning, a giant walked into the valley.
Over nine feet tall, in the Hebrew text.
And every morning, he shouted the same thing.
Give me a man to fight!
For forty days, nobody moved.
King Saul was terrified. The whole army was terrified.
Then a shepherd boy showed up with lunch for his brothers.
His name was David.
He heard the giant, and asked one question.
Who is he, that he should defy the armies of the living God?
Saul said, you're just a boy.
David said, God saved me from the lion and the bear.
He'll save me from this giant too.
Saul gave him his armor. David took it off.
He went down to the brook.
Five smooth stones.
The giant mocked him.
David shouted back.
The battle is the LORD's!
Then he ran toward the giant.
One stone.
Right in the forehead.
And the giant fell facedown.
No sword in David's hand.
Just a boy who knew how big his God was.
So what giant are you facing today?

dn.title: Daniel in the Lions' Den
dn.look: B: night silhouette-toon, rim light, slow and dramatic
lines: The new law said: for thirty days, pray to anyone but the king, and you go to the lions.
Daniel heard about the law.
Then he went home, and opened his windows toward Jerusalem.
He got down on his knees, and prayed.
Three times a day. Just as he had done before.
His enemies were watching.
The king loved Daniel. But even he couldn't change his own law.
So they threw Daniel into the den of lions.
May your God deliver you, the king said.
A stone was placed over the mouth of the den, and sealed.
That night, the king couldn't eat. He couldn't sleep.
At the first light of dawn, he hurried to the den.
Daniel! Has your God been able to deliver you?
And out of the dark, a voice answered.
My God sent His angel and shut the mouths of the lions.
Not one wound was found on him.
Because he had trusted in his God.
Daniel didn't start praying to get out of the den.
He was praying long before he ever went in.
So when you're in the den, who do you talk to?

el.title: Elijah and the Fire from Heaven
el.look: C: comic-book halftone, bold outlines, fastest cuts
lines: Four hundred fifty prophets. Against one.
The deal was simple.
Two altars. Two bulls. No fire.
The God who answers by fire, He is God.
Baal's prophets went first.
Morning. Noon. Shouting. Dancing.
O Baal, answer us!
Nothing.
So Elijah started teasing them.
Shout louder! Maybe he's asleep!
Still nothing.
Then Elijah rebuilt the LORD's altar.
Twelve stones.
And then he did something wild.
He soaked it with water. Three times.
Water filled the trench.
Then he prayed one short prayer.
Answer me, O LORD! Answer me.
Fire fell.
It burned the sacrifice, the wood, the stones, even the dust.
And licked up the water in the trench.
The people fell facedown.
The LORD, He is God!
All that shouting got no answer.
One prayer to the living God did.
So who are you calling on today?

pt.title: Peter Walks on Water
pt.look: D: storybook pastel, soft light, gentle tempo
lines: Have you ever stepped out in faith, and then started to sink?
It was the middle of the night.
The disciples were rowing hard, and the wind was against them.
Then they saw someone walking on the water.
It's a ghost, they cried!
But Jesus spoke up at once.
Take courage! It is I. Do not be afraid.
Peter said, Lord, if it is You, command me to come to You on the water.
And Jesus said one word.
Come.
So Peter stepped out of the boat.
And he walked on the water.
Then he saw the strength of the wind.
And he began to sink.
Lord, save me!
Immediately, Jesus reached out His hand and took hold of him.
Not after a lecture. Immediately.
Peter was the only one who got out of the boat.
And even when he sank, Jesus didn't let him go under.
If you're sinking right now, you only need three words.
Lord, save me.

pr.title: The Prodigal Son
pr.look: E: bright paper cut-out, flat colours, bouncy
lines: He asked his father for his share of the inheritance. Early.
Then he packed up, and left for a distant country.
And he blew it all on wild living.
Then a famine hit.
He ended up feeding pigs.
So hungry, he wanted to eat the pigs' food.
Then he came to his senses.
My father's servants have plenty to eat. And here I am, starving!
So he practiced a speech.
Father, I have sinned against heaven and against you.
I'm not worthy to be your son. Just make me a servant.
But while he was still a long way off, his father saw him.
And ran.
A wealthy father, running down the road.
He hugged him and kissed him, before the son could even finish.
Bring the best robe! A ring! Sandals!
This son of mine was dead, and is alive again!
He was lost, and is found!
Jesus told this story to show us what God is like.
No matter how far you've run, He's watching the road.
